explanations: terra: Earth is made a resting spread and sky a canopy, followed by provision; the human body's standing-place and covering are explicitly supplied by God.

luna: The section moves from human creation to return; this verse asks how people can disbelieve in God after death, life, death again, and return to Him. | terra: God gives life to the dead, causes death, gives life again, and to Him people are returned; the whole bodily circuit belongs to one sustaining hand.
terra: Adam and his spouse are made to descend, with earth assigned as settlement and temporary provision; human life begins on the very ground to which the body returns.
terra: The command to descend to earth is followed by promised guidance and freedom from fear for those who follow it, giving the earthly descent its faithful boundary.
terra: Those who disbelieve and deny the signs become companions of the Fire, completing the same descent passage with the opposite outcome.
terra: The House is made a place of return and security, and Abraham's standing-place a place of prayer; return, safety, and q-w-m converge at the sanctuary.

luna: The section swears by “this secure city”; Abraham asks God to make “this city” safe and provide its people, giving a prayer counterpart to the same البلد. | terra: Abraham asks that this be a secure بَلَد and that believers receive provision; the reply grants a disbeliever brief enjoyment before driving him to Fire, joining safe ground, sustenance, and final descent.

luna: The section’s root note gives the one-time act of rising upright; this command to “stand” (وَقُومُوا) before God uses that bodily sense in prayer. | terra: Believers are commanded to stand before God devoutly, making created upright posture an act of worship before its final judicial form.

luna: The section names al-Qayyūm in its dictionary account of resurrection; this verse calls God الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ, the living Sustainer, grounding the human’s support in the One who sustains. | terra: ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ neither slumbers nor sleeps and possesses all things, giving the q-w-m root its supreme sustaining referent behind every dependent upright creature.

luna: The section connects al-balad with bodies returned to earth; this verse opens at a town fallen upon its roofs, then recounts God reviving a dead man and his mount, joining a ruined place with bodily return to life. | terra: A ruined town lies collapsed on its roofs, a man is made to die and restored, and his bones are raised and clothed with flesh; fallen structure and reconstructed body illuminate one another.
luna: The section describes a human brought to a fitting form; this verse says God shapes people in their mothers’ wombs as He wills.
luna: The section’s q-w-m root carries the sense of what stands and sustains; this verse describes God as قائمًا بالقسط, upholding justice, a moral use of that uprightness.
terra: The same divine hand gives and removes rule, honors and abases; this rank reversal closely matches the section's hand that supports and lowers.
terra: God raises Jesus and places his followers above disbelievers until resurrection, then all return for judgment; raising, rank, return, and verdict form one promise.
terra: Adam's likeness begins from dust before God's creative command, a concise origin-from-ground counterpart to the body's eventual return.
terra: Abraham's standing-place and the safety of whoever enters the sanctuary meet in one ayah, linking q-w-m's place-form to the secure city.
terra: People once stood on the brink of a pit of Fire, but God saved them as they held His rope together; divine and communal support prevent the terminal fall.

luna: The section’s q-w-m root includes standing; this verse names people remembering God while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides as they reflect on creation. | terra: Remembering God while standing, sitting, and lying on one's side distinguishes qiyām as a concrete bodily posture among the alternatives implied by the section.

luna: The section’s dictionary form قِوَام (what a thing stands by) names support; 4:5 calls property قِيَامًا لَكُمْ, a support for people’s lives, giving that secondary root sense a direct Quranic use. | terra: Wealth is called what God made قِيَٰمًا for people, a direct Quranic use of the q-w-m family for the means by which human life is supported.
luna: The section describes a human made in the best upright form; this verse names the human’s weakness, a bodily limit beside that well-formed beginning.

luna: The section’s dictionary form قِوَام means support; this verse uses قَوَّامُونَ for those responsible for maintaining others, a social rather than bodily form of support. | terra: قَوَّٰمُونَ names an ongoing human maintenance responsibility and grounds it partly in spending, another concrete social use of the root for sustaining others.

luna: The section’s q-w-m root includes literal standing; this verse names remembering God while standing, sitting, or lying on one’s sides after prayer. | terra: After prayer, believers remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides; the repeated posture triad confirms the root's simplest physical sense.

luna: The section’s root note makes uprightness more than bodily form; this verse commands believers to be قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ, standing firmly for justice even against themselves or kin. | terra: The command كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ turns sustained uprightness into a stance for justice even against oneself and kin.

luna: The section’s أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ places a human at the lowest depth; this verse uses the same root in الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ for hypocrites’ lowest level in the Fire. | terra: The section cites the hypocrites in ٱلدَّرْكِ ٱلْأَسْفَلِ of the Fire, giving esfel an eschatological depth below bodily and social lowness.

luna: The section’s root note joins standing with support; this verse commands believers to be قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ and witnesses in justice, extending uprightness into conduct. | terra: Believers are commanded to be قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ as witnesses in justice, another moral stance held upright despite hostility.
terra: The crow scratches the earth to show Cain how to cover his brother's corpse, supplying the Quran's first concrete scene of a human body being put into the ground.
terra: God makes the Kaaba قِيَٰمًا لِّلنَّاسِ, a sustaining order for people; it expands the section's 'that by which a thing stands' from body to community.
terra: God creates people from clay and fixes both a life-term and an appointed term with Him, yet the addressees still doubt; earth-origin leads directly to judgment-denial.
terra: Deniers are made to stand before their Lord, acknowledge the truth, and face punishment; rejected judgment becomes an actual presentation.
terra: Punishment can come from above or from beneath people's feet, marking both sides of the vertical boundary on which the section's bodily image rests.
terra: God makes humans successors in earth and raises some over others in degrees to test them, distinguishing divinely assigned rank from moral worth.

luna: The section depicts a body brought to its completed standing form; this verse pairs creating and fashioning humanity with the command to the angels to prostrate to Adam. | terra: God says He created and then fashioned humankind before commanding the angels to prostrate to Adam; the formed body opens the same Adamic posture-scene as 15:29.
terra: Satan is ordered to descend because proud self-exaltation has no place there and is told to leave among the abased, joining direction, arrogance, and low rank.
terra: The command ٱهْبِطُوا۟ sends humans down, and earth becomes their settlement and provision for a term, explicitly binding descent to the human ground.
terra: On earth people live, die, and from it are brought forth; the ayah completes the descent of 7:24 with the same grave-and-second-rise circle as the section.
terra: Rain is driven to a dead بَلَد and revives it, and the ayah says 'thus We bring out the dead'; the land-word's ground sense becomes an explicit resurrection analogy.
terra: Good land brings forth vegetation by its Lord's leave while bad land yields only scant growth; the same ground bears opposed outcomes according to its condition.

luna: The section connects bodily descent to 7:176, where a man inclines to earth; this preceding verse introduces him as one who sheds the signs he had been given. | terra: This preceding ayah identifies the man in 7:176 as one given signs who stripped himself from them; it supplies the lost support that makes his earthward fall a denial-scene.

luna: The section itself names this scene: a man who could have been raised by the signs instead clings to earth (أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ), a direct reversal of elevation and descent. | terra: The section itself identifies the exact reversal: God could have raised the sign-bearer, but he أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ, clung to earth; bodily height and ground-contact expose the spiritual fall into denial.
luna: The section links 7:176’s earth-bound man with denial; this next verse calls the example of those who deny God’s signs and wrong themselves an evil one, completing that warning.

luna: The section’s well-formed human can be lowered; this verse says people who fail to use their hearts, eyes, and ears are like cattle, even further astray. | terra: People who refuse to use their created faculties become like cattle, indeed further astray; fine human equipment can terminate in a rank below the creaturely comparison.
terra: The deaf and speechless who do not reason are called the worst creatures before God, a moral low rank reached despite human form.
terra: When called to rise and go forth, people ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ and prefer worldly life; this is the closest nonlexical repeat of choosing to cling heavily to earth.
terra: God makes the disbelievers' word ٱلسُّفْلَىٰ while His word is ٱلْعُلْيَا, an explicit rank-pair that confirms the section's upper/lower moral register.
terra: The command وَلَا تَقُمْ عَلَىٰ قَبْرِهِ places standing and the grave in one scene, while the dead person's disbelief makes it a pointed boundary for the section's faith exception.

luna: The section’s root note names a support that keeps something from falling; this verse contrasts a foundation on piety with one at a crumbling edge that collapses with its builder into the Fire. | terra: A building founded on reverence is opposed to one on a collapsing brink that falls with its builder into Hell; sound support and final downward collapse form the whole comparison.
terra: The return of all to God is guaranteed because He begins and repeats creation; the repeated creation then separates righteous believers' reward from deniers' punishment.
terra: Those content with worldly life, at rest in it, and heedless of the signs enact the earth-bound satisfaction that precedes denial's low end.
terra: Fire is their refuge because of what they earned, completing the passage's movement from worldly contentment to final abasement.
terra: When hardship touches a person he calls on God lying, sitting, or standing, then passes on after relief; shifting bodily states accompany forgetfulness of the sustaining hand.
terra: God produced humans from earth and settled them in it, then calls them to seek forgiveness and return; earth is both origin, habitation, and setting for moral response.
terra: The punished town's upper part is made its lower part, عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا; the built structure is literally overturned across the same high/low axis developed in the section.
terra: The blessed remain in the Garden with عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ, a gift not cut off, an especially close nonlexical counterpart to ghayr mamnūn.
terra: When Joseph's shirt reaches Jacob's face, he returns to seeing; فَٱرْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا is an exact bodily example of r-d-d restoring a prior condition.

luna: The section’s dictionary note says a support keeps a thing standing; this verse speaks of God raising the heavens without visible pillars, an elevated structure whose support is not seen. | terra: God raises the heavens بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا, without visible pillars; height immediately raises the question of the support by which something elevated remains standing.
terra: The deniers' astonished question asks whether after becoming dust they will enter a new creation; the ayah then names them deniers of their Lord.
terra: The Garden's food and shade are lasting, a concrete statement of the continuance conveyed by ghayr mamnūn.

luna: The section describes height that depends on support; this verse pictures a good word as a tree with a firm root and branches reaching high, a clear image of rooted support and elevation. | terra: A good word is a good tree whose root is firm and branch reaches heaven, a living image of upright height sustained from below and bearing continuing fruit.

luna: The section’s dictionary form قِوَام means what holds a thing up; this verse contrasts the firmly rooted tree with a bad word like a tree uprooted from the earth, having no stability. | terra: An evil word is an uprooted tree with no stability in the earth, showing how loss of grounding turns apparent height into collapse.

luna: The section asks what keeps a human standing; this next verse says God makes believers firm with a firm word in worldly life and the Hereafter, continuing the tree parable’s concern with stability.

luna: The section names “this secure city”; Abraham’s prayer uses البلد and asks that it be safe, matching the city’s particular scene. | terra: Abraham's prayer رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ ءَامِنًا is the closest repeated formulation of the section's 'this secure city.'
terra: On the day of warning people rush with heads raised while their gaze لَا يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ; the return-root now describes an eye unable to come back under terror.
terra: When earth and heavens are exchanged, everyone appears before the One God; even the body's ground is remade for the final presentation.

luna: The section describes the human as fashioned in a fitting form; this verse says God fashioned Adam and breathed into him of His spirit, followed by the command to prostrate. | terra: Once Adam is proportioned and given spirit, the angels must prostrate; bodily completion becomes the threshold of a deliberate descent before the formed human.
terra: This repeated account again makes the town's عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا, supplying a second direct occurrence of top becoming bottom.

luna: The section’s support image is made concrete here: God placed firm mountains in the earth so it would not shake with people, alongside rivers and paths. | terra: Firm mountains are cast into earth lest it shift with people, directly showing the standing-ground secured against collapse.
terra: God attacks a building from its foundations so its roof falls upon its occupants from above; withdrawn support converts the upper structure into a downward blow.

luna: The section’s upright body can descend into frailty; this verse says some are returned to decrepit age, knowing little after having known much. | terra: After creating people, God takes them in death, and some are يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ; the same return-root and a bodily descent into decrepitude closely enact being returned from fine formation to a low condition.
terra: God brings people from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing and grants hearing, sight, and hearts, yet little gratitude follows; bestowed equipment can end in moral failure.

luna: The section’s reward is غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, not cut off; this verse contrasts what passes away with what remains with God, clarifying the durability of that reward. | terra: What people possess runs out while what is with God remains, and the patient receive their reward; this states in other words what 'uncut' reward adds to the image.
terra: A city secure and tranquil with abundant provision becomes clothed in hunger and fear after ingratitude; the secure ground is reversed by moral failure.
terra: The Quran guides لِلَّتِى هِىَ أَقْوَمُ and promises believers who do good a great reward, moving the upright-root from bodily form to the way that sustains a life.
terra: Worldly preference already creates ranks, but the Hereafter has greater degrees and preference; final rank exceeds visible bodily and social height.
luna: The section’s 95:5, 95:6, and 95:7 turn from bodily form to judgment; this verse voices the same objection about whether bones and fragments can be raised as a new creation.
terra: When skeptics ask who will restore them, the answer is the One who formed them the first time; first bodily formation is the warrant for return.
terra: God honors Adam's children, carries and provides for them, and favors them over much creation; this states the bestowed human rank surrounding 'best formation.'
terra: The condemned are gathered on their faces, blind, mute, and deaf, with Hell as refuge; honored human faculties and upright carriage are comprehensively reversed.
terra: Those given knowledge fall on their faces in prostration when revelation is recited, making bodily descent the truthful answer to God's signs.
terra: Those who recognize revelation fall on their faces weeping and increase in humility, completing the truthful bodily response begun in 17:107.
terra: God places no عِوَجًا, crookedness, in the Book; this is the removal of crookedness half of the section's definition of setting something upright.
terra: قَيِّمًا completes 18:1: the Book is upright, warns of severe punishment, and announces good reward to believers who do good.
luna: The section’s 95:7 questions denial of judgment; this neighboring verse states the garden owner’s denial of the Hour, while 18:37 answers with the human’s creation from dust and a drop.

luna: The section asks what follows the human’s finely fashioned body; the garden owner’s companion says God created him from dust, then a drop, then fashioned him as a man, and challenges his denial. | terra: The section cites the rebuke to the garden owner: God created him from dust and a drop, then سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلًا; the completed man's stance is invoked against his disbelief.
terra: The disbelieving garden owner's crop is destroyed and its trellised growth lies collapsed, so the rebuke about the One who formed him in 18:37 ends in a visible loss of support.

luna: The section promises believers an uncut reward for righteous deeds; this verse calls lasting good works better than worldly wealth and children for reward and hope. | terra: Wealth and children are passing adornment, while enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and hope; what passes is measured against what remains.
terra: People are presented before God in rows and told they have come as first created, making first formation and final standing one explicit judicial scene.
terra: Zechariah describes bones weakened and a head blazing with gray, giving the section's loss of bodily support a vivid first-person old-age form.
terra: Prophets and the guided خَرُّوا۟ سُجَّدًا وَبُكِيًّا when God's signs are recited; falling to earth here manifests elevated faith rather than degradation.
terra: Enduring righteous deeds are better with God in reward and return, repeating the lasting consequence of the faithful exception.
terra: Moses says he leans upon his staff, giving the support-object from Solomon's fall scene its ordinary bodily function.

luna: The section’s upright human is returned downward; Moses’ words give the full earth-cycle: God creates people from earth, returns them to it, then brings them out again. | terra: The section cites this complete earth-cycle: created from earth, returned into it, and brought out from it once more; the body that reaches the ground will be raised again.
luna: The section’s 95:7 asks why people deny after creation and return; this next verse says Pharaoh was shown the signs but denied them, continuing the passage about the earth-cycle in 20:55.
terra: Whoever comes as a believer with righteous deeds receives ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ, the high degrees, an explicit upper-rank counterpart to the section's low destination and faithful exception.
terra: At resurrection the mountains are removed and the ground is left a level plain, stripping the standing-place of its former elevations and supports.
terra: No crookedness or uneven rise can be seen in the leveled ground, a cosmic counterpart to removing crookedness and the final erasure of high/low terrain.
terra: Faces are humbled before ٱلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ; the One by whom creation subsists confronts lowered human faces, joining the support-sense of the root to the final standing.
terra: Humans are sent down together, but whoever follows divine guidance will neither stray nor suffer; descent to earth does not itself determine low moral rank.
terra: Firm mountains keep earth from shifting with its inhabitants, a repeated formulation of the support beneath embodied human movement.
terra: God promises to repeat creation just as He began the first creation, making the second formation answer directly to the first well-formed body.

luna: The section moves from a formed human to a lowered one; this verse traces the body from dust through womb and infant stages to maturity and frail old age, and pairs that with dead earth revived. | terra: This ayah joins creation from dust, embryonic formation, being returned to the most abject age, death, and revived earth as proof of resurrection; it contains nearly the whole section's rise-decline-ground-rise circuit.

luna: The section’s return to earth leads to a later rising; this next verse says the Hour is coming and God will raise those in the graves, completing the resurrection scene beside 22:5. | terra: God will raise those in the graves, directly turning the section's dictionary sense of balad as grave-ground into the place of bodily emergence.
terra: One who associates partners is likened to a person falling from the sky and carried off by birds or wind, giving loss of faith the section's unsupported bodily fall.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary sense for بلد describes a camel lowering its chest to the ground when it kneels; this verse says sacrificial camels fall onto their sides before they are eaten. It is a different kind of falling.
terra: Destroyed towns lie collapsed upon their roofs, repeating at civic scale the downward result of a structure losing what holds it up.

luna: The section names the support that keeps a thing from falling; this verse says God holds the sky lest it fall upon the earth, making the image of a sustaining hand concrete. | terra: God يُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَآءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ, holds the sky from falling to earth, staging the exact relation between support, fall, and the ground.

luna: The section starts from the completed human form; this verse gives its bodily beginning as an extract of clay, setting the human body within a creation sequence. | terra: Human creation begins from an extract of clay, giving the formed body in 23:14 its material origin in earth.

luna: The section’s upright body begins in a lowly origin; this verse says the human seed is placed in a secure lodging, between the clay origin in 23:12 and bodily formation in 23:14. | terra: The drop is placed in a firm lodging, a concrete support and enclosure within the process that produces the completed body in 23:14.

luna: The section describes a body brought to its finest form; this verse traces its formation through a clot, lump, bones, and flesh before calling it another creation. | terra: The embryo becomes bones, the bones are clothed with flesh, and it is produced as another creation; this makes the hidden construction behind the finished human body visible.
terra: God produces human hearing, sight, and hearts, followed by 'little are you grateful'; completed capacities do not guarantee an upright response.
luna: The section’s created body is lowered to earth; these deniers ask whether they will rise after dying, becoming dust and bones.
luna: The section’s 95:7 asks why people deny the recompense; this next verse says the deniers call the promise of resurrection a tale of the ancients.
terra: At death the human asks, 'My Lord, return me,' making r-d-d's restoration sense a desperate bodily request at the point of collapse.
terra: The requested return is refused, a barrier remains until resurrection, and the speaker's wish to do righteousness connects bodily return with the faithful exception.
terra: Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are called worst in place and most astray in path, merging bodily inversion with degraded final rank.
terra: Those who refuse to hear or reason become like cattle, indeed further astray, repeating the fall beneath the rank implied by human formation.
terra: Rain revives a dead بَلْدَة and waters animals and people, showing the land not only as the body's bottom surface but as the support that restores bodily life.

luna: The section’s root note describes upright standing; this verse pairs standing with prostration in the night worship of the servants of the Merciful. | terra: The servants of the Merciful spend the night prostrating and standing before their Lord, using both lowered and upright postures in faithful devotion.
terra: Balanced spending is قَوَامًا between extravagance and stinginess, extending the root from bodily poise to a measure that keeps conduct from leaning to either extreme.
luna: The section contrasts lowering with the reward for steadfast servants; this verse promises them lofty rooms in Paradise for their patience.
terra: Those who bring evil are thrown face-first into the Fire; the downward bodily orientation realizes their low moral outcome.
luna: The section names the secure city; this verse calls it البلدة whose Lord is to be worshipped and says He made it sacred, identifying the same kind of place.
terra: God wills to confer favor on those weakened in the earth and make them leaders and inheritors; the m-n-n family accompanies a divinely effected rise of the lowly into strength.
terra: A secure sanctuary receives provision from God, repeating the safe-ground and sustenance pairing without the word balad.
luna: The section’s body has a downward end while believers receive enduring recompense; this verse contrasts worldly provision with what remains with God and is better.
terra: The final abode is for those who do not desire عُلُوًّا in the earth; it marks a boundary between gifted uprightness and self-exalting rank.
luna: The section’s return to earth leads to another emergence; this verse asks whether people see that God begins creation and then repeats it.
luna: The section puts human creation and return on an earthly ground; this verse tells people to travel the earth, see how creation began, and recognize the later creation.
terra: Punishment covers deniers from above and from beneath their feet, enclosing the body between upper and lower rather than leaving its height secure.
luna: The section promises believers who do good a reward that is not cut off; this verse promises such believers secure upper rooms in Paradise and calls that an excellent reward.
terra: God makes a sanctuary secure while people are snatched away around it, then asks whether they believe in falsehood; physical security is again placed beside denial.

luna: The section’s body is formed and then sent downward; this verse says God begins creation, repeats it, and to Him people return. | terra: God begins creation, repeats it, and then people are returned to Him, compressing first formation, re-formation, and final return into one ayah.
terra: Creation from dust is followed by humans spreading across the earth, moving from low material origin to active embodied life.

luna: The section’s q-w-m root links standing and rising; here the heavens and earth stand by God’s command, then people emerge from the earth when called, joining support with resurrection. | terra: The heavens and earth تَقُومَانِ by God's command, then humans answer a call and emerge from earth; cosmic standing-by-support and bodily resurrection meet in one ayah.
terra: The command to set one's face to the religion joins God's human fiṭrah, no alteration in creation, and ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ; created form and moral uprightness meet explicitly.

luna: The section’s upright body has a downward arc; this verse explicitly moves human life from weakness to strength and back to weakness and old age. | terra: God makes weakness, then strength, then weakness and gray hair; this explicitly identifies the sustaining strength between two bodily low states and attributes every transition to the same Creator.

luna: The section says support is what keeps a thing upright; this verse says God set firm mountains in the earth lest it shake with people, a concrete stabilizing role. | terra: The heavens are created without visible pillars and stabilizing mountains are cast into earth lest it shift with people; cosmic and earthly supports frame the human standing-place.

luna: The section’s human is finely formed; this verse says God perfected what He created and began the human’s creation from clay. | terra: ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُ introduces human creation from clay, placing the section's 'best formation' within God's making creation well.
luna: The section’s formed body has an earthly beginning; this verse says humanity’s descendants come from an extract of a despised fluid, continuing the creation sequence.

luna: The section’s image is the completed human body; this verse says God fashioned the human and breathed into him of His spirit, then gave hearing, sight, and hearts. | terra: God proportions the human, breathes spirit, and grants hearing, sight, and hearts, yet people give little thanks; formed capacity is followed by a moral falling-short.
terra: Deniers ask whether, once ضَلَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ, lost into the earth, they can be newly created; bodily disappearance into ground is explicitly tied to denial of meeting the Lord.
terra: Criminals stand with heads bowed before their Lord and ask to be sent back; forced lowering at judgment contrasts with the confident upright form they once misused.
terra: True believers in the signs خَرُّوا۟ سُجَّدًا when reminded and are not arrogant; voluntary bodily lowering becomes the opposite of the denier's degrading fall.

terra: Solomon's dead body remains upright only through his staff; when the creature eats the staff he falls, a uniquely concrete Quranic scene of a body, its support, and the collapse that follows support's removal.
terra: A good land and forgiving Lord accompany two productive gardens and provision, showing balad as sustaining ground rather than merely a named city.
terra: When the people turn away, their fertile gardens are replaced after the flood by bitter, sparse growth; sustaining land visibly falls from good condition.

luna: The section’s exception turns on belief and righteous works; this verse says wealth and children do not bring nearness, but believers who do good receive multiplied reward and secure lofty chambers.
luna: The section’s q-w-m root names a bodily rising; this command tells the Prophet’s audience to stand for God singly or in pairs and then reflect.

luna: The section links human creation and return to the ground; this verse describes God reviving dead earth, a land-level counterpart to the body’s return and re-emergence. | terra: God revives a dead بَلَد with rain and concludes كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ, making dead land a direct figure for bodily rising.

luna: The section contrasts a human lowered with believers’ good works; this verse says good words ascend to God and righteous deeds raise them, giving deeds an upward trajectory. | terra: Good speech ascends to God and righteous action raises it, giving good deeds an upward movement opposite the denier's attachment to earth.
terra: Creation from dust and then a drop is followed by the measured span of every life, placing formed embodiment under the same power that limits its duration.
terra: Humans are the needy before God while God is self-sufficient and praiseworthy; this supplies the theological relation behind a body that cannot uphold itself.
terra: The living and dead are not equal, and the Prophet cannot make those in graves hear; grave-ground marks a present boundary that resurrection alone will reverse.

luna: The section’s dictionary note defines support as what prevents a thing from falling; 35:41 says God holds the heavens and earth lest they cease, an explicit cosmic instance of that sustaining role. | terra: God holds the heavens and earth أَن تَزُولَا, lest they slip or fall, and none can hold them after Him; this directly matches support that turns a thing back from collapse.
terra: At the trumpet people rush from the graves to their Lord; emergence from ground terminates in the standing for God developed through q-w-m.

luna: The section’s fall can be heard as bodily decline; this verse says a person given long life is reversed in creation until strength and knowledge recede. | terra: وَمَن نُّعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّسْهُ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ pictures long life as being reversed in bodily creation, a direct parallel to the upright body being turned downward.

luna: The section moves from a formed body to its return; this verse voices the objection that decomposed bones cannot be brought back to life. | terra: The disputant forgets his own creation and asks who will revive decayed bones, making denial arise from failure to read the formed body backward to its Maker.

luna: The section’s body is returned and raised; this answer says the One who made it the first time will give life to the bones, completing 36:78. | terra: The answer says the One who originated the bones the first time will revive them, linking first formation directly to second formation.

luna: The section’s secondary dictionary sense for بلد uses an exposed ostrich egg as an image of lowliness; this verse’s بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ are concealed eggs, reversing exposure into protection. The Qur’an does not specify an ostrich.
terra: Abraham's opponents intend to dominate him, but God makes them ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ; the low rank is a divinely effected reversal, not merely a spatial description.
terra: God's provision in the Hereafter has no exhaustion, مَا لَهُۥ مِن نَّفَادٍ, another explicit boundary against a reward that ends.

luna: The section’s upright human recalls the completed formation of Adam; this verse says God fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, then commands the angels to prostrate. | terra: The parallel command repeats فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ and the breathing of spirit before prostration, confirming the completed upright human scene beyond its first telling.

luna: The section’s root note names standing upright; this verse describes a worshipper prostrating and standing while fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy. | terra: The devout person spends the night prostrating and standing while fearing the Hereafter, a faithful alternation of lowered and upright postures rather than a degrading fall.
terra: The patient are paid their reward without reckoning, extending the faithful exception toward a gift unbounded by ordinary measure.
luna: The section names the lowest depth as a fate; this verse promises believers lofty, built chambers above one another, a specific elevated counterpart.
terra: God takes souls at death and sleep, retains those decreed to die, and sends the others back for a term; the same hand withholds and restores bodily life.
terra: After the second trumpet blast, the dead are قِيَامٌ يَنظُرُونَ, standing and looking; this is the section's second upright posture after bodily return.

luna: The section’s human stands in the best form; this verse says God fashioned people and made their forms good, alongside making earth a settled place. | terra: Earth is made a settlement, heaven a structure, and human forms are made good; the ayah joins the body's fine form to the ground and built support imagery surrounding it.

luna: The section’s body moves from creation toward decline; this verse traces people from dust and a drop through childhood and maturity to old age and death. | terra: Creation from dust passes through embryo, childhood, maturity, old age, and death; this full bodily arc supplies the temporal descent implicit between finest formation and return.

luna: The section notes that مَمْنُون means cut off and names مَنّة as sustaining strength; this verse promises believers who do good an أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, an uncut reward. | terra: Believers who do good receive أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, the same uncut-reward formula as the section's exception.
terra: The condemned ask to put their human and jinn misleaders beneath their feet so they become مِنَ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ; physical underfoot position and degraded rank coincide.
terra: Those who say 'Our Lord is God' and then ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟ are promised freedom from fear and the Garden; steadfast uprightness realizes the faithful exception.
terra: Measured water revives a dead بَلْدَة, followed by كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ; the same ground that receives becomes the image of being brought out.
terra: God raises some people above others in degrees so that they may take one another in service, showing social height as an interdependent support-order rather than self-sufficiency.
luna: The section’s final question challenges denial of judgment; this verse gives the claim that life ends with death and time alone, the denial to which 45:26 replies.
luna: The section’s body returns and is raised; this next verse says deniers demand their forefathers be brought back, completing the challenge in 45:24.
luna: The section asks what makes people deny judgment after creation; this next verse answers that God gives life and death and will gather people on the Day of Resurrection.
terra: Those who say God is their Lord and then ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟ have no fear or grief; it repeats the faithful consequence of remaining upright.
luna: The section divides human outcomes by what people do; this verse says each person will have degrees according to their deeds, linking action with rank at judgment.
terra: The believers are likened to a crop that strengthens its shoots, thickens, and stands upright on its stems; mutual support produces a mature upright form.

luna: The section returns the human to earth; this verse records deniers asking whether they will be recreated after death and becoming dust. | terra: The objection أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا rejects a bodily return from dust as remote, placing the section's earthward return at the center of resurrection denial.
luna: The section’s earthly return is not the final state; this next verse says God knows what the earth diminishes of them and keeps a record.
terra: A dead بَلْدَة is given life and the ayah concludes كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ, explicitly joining land and emergence.
luna: The section joins the first human creation to the final return; this verse rejects the idea that God was unable to create first and says people doubt the new creation.
terra: The earth splits away from people as they hasten out, a direct picture of ground releasing the bodies returned to it.
terra: With humbled eyes, people emerge from graves like scattered locusts; lowered faces and upward emergence appear in the same resurrection body.
terra: The criminals are dragged on their faces into the Fire, a literal final lowering of bodies that rejected resurrection.

luna: The section describes human proportion and an upright form; this verse speaks of the raised sky and the balance set in creation, pairing height with measured order. | terra: God raises the heaven and sets the balance, joining height to the measured order that keeps it from becoming distortion.
luna: The section’s تقويم describes setting things right; this next verse commands that the balance not be transgressed, continuing the raised-sky and balance image of 55:7.

luna: The section’s form is made upright and proportioned; this next verse commands just measure and forbids reducing the balance, completing the measured-order passage. | terra: The command وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ uses the standing-root for maintaining just measure, a nonbodily analogue to corrected, balanced form.
luna: The section lowers a created human and promises believers a lasting reward; this verse says all who are upon the earth perish, the mortal side of that contrast.
luna: The section’s human body is lowered while its reward is uncut; this verse says the Lord of Majesty and Honor remains, the enduring side of the contrast begun in 55:26.

luna: The section’s high-to-low movement has an explicit counterpart in this verse: the Event lowers some and raises others, describing a reversal of rank. | terra: The coming event is خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ, lowering some and raising others; it states the final two-way rank reversal latent in the section's vertical axis.
terra: Paradise fruit is لَا مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلَا مَمْنُوعَةٍ, neither cut off nor withheld, making the section's 'uncut' reward sensuous without sharing the m-n-n form.
luna: The section asks what becomes of the body lowered to earth; these deniers ask whether they will be raised after dying and becoming dust and bones.
luna: The section’s image concerns the body’s return and reappearance; this next verse extends the deniers’ question to their forefathers, completing the challenge in 56:47.
luna: The section places death within a return to God; this verse commands the answer that the former and later generations will all be gathered.
luna: The section’s descent does not end in disappearance; this next verse says the gathered generations meet at an appointed time, completing 56:49.
luna: The section gives earth as the body’s destination; this verse says God revives the earth after its death, a specific parallel to bodies emerging after return to earth.

luna: The section’s image of a human held upright meets a moral use of the q-w-m family here: messengers and the Balance are sent so people may uphold justice. | terra: Revelation and the balance are sent so that people لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلْقِسْطِ, making 'standing' the establishment of a just human order.

luna: The section’s high-to-low body is reversed here: believers and the learned are raised in rank, and the command انشزوا tells people to rise when asked. | terra: God raises believers and people of knowledge by degrees; this is the faithful upward counter-movement to being placed among the low.

terra: The hypocrites' impressive bodies are likened to خُشُبٌ مُّسَنَّدَةٌ, propped timbers; external uprightness depends on a support while inwardly they are lifeless, sharpening the section's distinction between form and final rank.

luna: The section’s body is made in a fitting form; this verse says God created and shaped people and made their forms good. | terra: God formed people and made their forms good, وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ, then states that the destination is to Him; good form and final return are held together.

luna: The section’s 95:7 asks what can make a person deny judgment; this verse directly answers deniers who claim they will not be raised after death, saying they will be raised and informed of their deeds.
terra: God creates death and life to test who is best in deeds; 'best' shifts from received bodily form to the action by which that form is answered.
terra: God makes earth tractable for walking and provision, then says resurrection is to Him; the supporting ground of life leads directly to emergence.

luna: The section sets the upright body against a downward fate; this verse contrasts one walking fallen on his face with one walking upright on a straight path, making bodily posture a figure of guidance. | terra: The face-down walker مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ is set against one who walks سَوِيًّا on a straight path, turning the section's upright-versus-lowered body into a moral and eschatological contrast.
terra: The Creator produces people and gives hearing, sight, and hearts, but they give little thanks; human formation and human failure stand side by side.
terra: God promises the Prophet أَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ, preserving the same uncut reward while changing the immediate addressee.
terra: On the day people are summoned to prostrate, they cannot do so; the once-sound upright body has lost the capacity for faithful voluntary lowering.
terra: Eyes are humbled and humiliation covers those who were called to prostrate while sound, distinguishing chosen prostration in life from forced abasement at judgment.
terra: People emerge rapidly from graves as though racing toward a marker, giving the second rising a forceful bodily movement.
terra: God has created people in successive stages, supplying the developmental movement between earthly origin and the return-and-emergence of 71:17-18.

luna: The section connects the body’s return with the ground; this verse says God caused people to grow from the earth like plants, giving the return-to-earth image a creation-side counterpart. | terra: God caused humankind to grow from earth like a growth; read with 71:18, origin in the ground precedes return into and emergence from it.

luna: The section’s downward return is one phase of a larger cycle; this verse says God will return people to earth and bring them forth again. | terra: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا states both return into earth and forceful emergence from it, matching descent to the ground and the second rising.
terra: The Prophet is told not to give or remind of a favor seeking increase; this distinct m-n-n sense sets human calculated giving against God's uncut reward.

luna: The section asks what follows the body’s lowering; this verse presents the denier’s doubt that God can gather his bones. | terra: Humanity asks whether God will gather its bones, a direct denial of the body's reassembly after its collapse.

luna: The section’s body is formed with a particular stature; this answer says God can restore even the fingertips, completing the challenge about reassembling bones. | terra: God answers that He can proportion even the fingertips, carrying fine bodily formation through death into exact re-formation.
terra: People love the immediate life, naming the temporal preference behind the earthward attachment.
terra: They leave the Hereafter, completing the boundary between passing nearness and enduring reward.
terra: At death the life reaches the collarbones, locating the body's loss of strength within the body itself.
terra: One leg is entwined with the other, a vivid image of the formerly upright body's support failing at death.
terra: On that day the drive is toward the Lord, turning bodily collapse into the unavoidable final return.
terra: The human was first a discharged drop, supplying the low material beginning for the created and proportioned body in 75:38.
terra: From a clot God خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ, created and proportioned the human; the wording directly parallels the section's account of making the body fit.
terra: After recalling first formation, the passage asks whether its Maker can revive the dead; fine form becomes the direct proof of re-formation.
terra: God creates the human from a mixed drop in order to test him and equips him with hearing and sight; fine formation is explicitly ordered toward moral trial.
terra: Guidance leaves the formed human either grateful or ungrateful, clarifying how one created form can lead to the section's opposed final ranks.
luna: The section describes a human body fashioned and held upright; this verse says God created people and strengthened their frames, and can replace them with others like them.
luna: The section starts from the human body made in a fitting form; this verse recalls its creation from a lowly fluid, giving the formed body an explicit, humble beginning.
luna: The section’s root note says a body needs support to remain upright; this next verse places the human fluid in a firm lodging, a specific image of bodily support.
luna: The section describes a body given its proper form; this next verse says the fluid remains in that lodging for a known term, completing the gestation sequence begun in 77:20–21.
luna: The section’s image of proportioned bodily form meets this next verse’s language of measuring or decreeing the creation, which concludes the sequence of 77:20–22.
terra: God asks whether He made earth كِفَاتًا, a containing receptacle, making the ground a support and enclosure.
terra: أَحْيَآءً وَأَمْوَٰتًا specifies that the earth of 77:25 gathers both living and dead bodies.

luna: The section connects the body with earth as its resting ground; this verse calls the earth a bed, a specific image of the surface that supports life. | terra: Earth is made a resting-place, the broad support beneath the upright human body.

luna: The section’s dictionary form قِوَام names what keeps a thing standing; this next verse calls mountains pegs, an explicit support image continuing the earth-as-bed scene in 78:6. | terra: Mountains are made pegs, completing 78:6's ground with the image of what fixes and stabilizes it.
luna: The section returns the human body to the lowest; this verse says the disbeliever, seeing his deeds on the warned-of Day, will wish he were dust.
terra: The skeptics ask whether they will be لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِى ٱلْحَافِرَةِ, returned to the former state; r-d-d here names resurrection as restoration.
terra: The objection 'when we are decayed bones?' supplies the bodily condition from which the return questioned in 79:10 must occur.
terra: A single blast is sufficient for resurrection, the initiating act whose bodily result appears in the next ayah.
terra: After the blast, people are suddenly upon the earth's surface, an especially concise emergence from below to above.
luna: The section sends the human down from a high standing; Pharaoh’s nearby claim “I am your highest lord” is followed by punishment in 79:25, exposing the reversal of self-exaltation.
luna: The section centers on the human’s fitted form; this verse explicitly compares the difficulty of creating people with creating the heaven, before describing the heaven’s raised structure.

luna: The section describes a body standing in its best proportion; this next verse says the heaven was raised and proportioned, continuing the creation comparison in 79:27. | terra: God raises the heaven's canopy and proportions it, transferring the section's two linked acts—elevation and setting right—from the body to a structure.
luna: The section’s body is lowered to an earthly ground; this verse says the earth was spread out, an explicit counterpart to that ground.
luna: The section names a support that keeps a body standing; this verse says God firmly set the mountains, a specific instance of stabilizing support in the earth scene.

luna: The section’s descent follows a moral distinction; this passage begins with the one who transgresses, whose outcome is spelled out in the next verses. | terra: The passage first identifies the one who transgressed, beginning the downward moral sequence that culminates in Fire.

luna: The section’s low outcome can follow a person’s choice; this next verse says the transgressor preferred the nearer life, completing the description begun in 79:37. | terra: Preferring the nearer life supplies the concrete choice behind the transgressor's low outcome.

luna: The section names the low outcome as “lowest of the low”; this next verse makes the nearer-life preference end in Hell, opposite the garden promised to those who fear God in 79:41. | terra: Hell becomes the transgressor's refuge, the lower eschatological terminus of preferring worldly life.

luna: The section’s q-w-m root names standing before God; this verse describes one who fears standing before his Lord and restrains the self, giving the upright stance a judgment context. | terra: The opposite person fears the standing before his Lord and restrains the self from desire; q-w-m's judicial sense produces an upright moral response.

luna: The section’s believers and doers of good receive an uncut reward; this next verse says the Garden is the refuge of the one who feared God’s standing and restrained desire. | terra: The Garden becomes that person's refuge, completing the faithful upward alternative to 79:39.
luna: The section describes a human created in a fitted form; this neighboring passage asks from what a person was created, introducing its bodily sequence.
luna: The section’s تقويم is the human made upright and well-proportioned; this verse says God created and proportioned the person, a direct parallel in a passage about life’s stages.

luna: The section’s body returns downward; this verse says God causes the person to die and be buried, giving the descent a literal bodily endpoint. | terra: God causes the human to die and assigns him a grave, the precise bodily lodging suggested by the section's secondary sense of balad.

luna: The section’s descent is not the end of the human course; this verse says God will raise the person again, continuing the death and burial of 80:21. | terra: ثُمَّ إِذَا شَآءَ أَنشَرَهُ reverses 80:21's burial by raising the same human when God wills.
luna: The section moves from a made body to its final division; this verse shows one group’s faces bright on that Day, beginning the bodily contrast completed by the dusty faces in 80:40 and 80:41.
luna: The section distinguishes the faithful from those lowered; this next verse says the bright faces are smiling and rejoicing, continuing the group in 80:38.
luna: The section’s low outcome is bodily; this verse shows other faces covered with dust, the opposite appearance to 80:38 and the beginning of their fate in 80:41 and 80:42.
luna: The section’s low end is contrasted with a faithful exception; this next verse says darkness covers the dusty faces of 80:40, continuing that group’s outcome.
luna: The section’s downward outcome follows from denial; this next verse identifies the faces in 80:40 and 80:41 as those of disbelievers and sinners.
terra: The message is for whoever wills أَن يَسْتَقِيمَ, carrying the bodily root into the human choice to take a straight course.
terra: When the graves are overturned and their contents scattered, the ground no longer holds the lowered bodies placed within it.
terra: The question asks the human what deceived him concerning his generous Lord, framing the bodily forming in 82:7-8 and denial in 82:9 as one rebuke.

luna: The section’s 95:4 speaks of creating and proportioning the human; this verse says God created, fashioned, and balanced the person, a direct account of bodily form. | terra: The section cites the Creator who خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ, directly restating creation as bodily proportioning and balancing.

luna: The section’s image concerns a body given its form; this next verse says God composed the human in whatever form He willed, completing the bodily shaping in 82:7. | terra: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ completes 82:7 by locating that proportion in the deliberately assembled human form.

luna: The section’s 95:7 asks what makes a person deny judgment after being created; this next verse says, “Rather, you deny the Recompense,” following the formation in 82:7 and 82:8. | terra: The abrupt answer كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ makes denial of judgment the response to fine formation, exactly the sequence the section highlights.
luna: The section’s lowest outcome is separated from the exception for faith and good deeds; this verse places the righteous in bliss, the positive side of that division.
luna: The section’s lowest outcome follows the formed human; this next verse says the wicked are in Hell, the opposite of the righteous in 82:13.
luna: The section asks what makes people deny judgment; this next verse says the wicked will burn there on the Day of Recompense, specifying when the fate of 82:14 occurs.

luna: The section recalls standing before God on the Day of Resurrection; this preceding verse asks whether those who cheat in measure expect to be raised. The next verse calls it a great day, and 83:6 says people stand before the Lord. | terra: The question أَلَا يَظُنُّ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَنَّهُم مَّبْعُوثُونَ introduces the resurrection whose bodily standing is shown in 83:6.

luna: The section’s bodily standing recalls judgment; this verse calls the resurrection day a great day, and the next verse, 83:6, says people stand before the Lord of the worlds. | terra: This ayah names the setting as a tremendous day, giving the standing in 83:6 its judicial scale even though it does not itself picture the posture.

luna: The section’s q-w-m root names standing and resurrection; this verse says people stand before the Lord of the worlds on the day that judges those who cheated in measure. | terra: The section cites يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلنَّاسُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ: the root of bodily setting-upright culminates in all people standing for their Lord.
luna: The section’s 95:5 and 95:6 divide people by their end; this continuation of 83:6 says the record of the wicked is in Sijjin, introducing their fate after the standing for judgment.
luna: The section sets the low outcome against the faithful exception; this passage places the record of the righteous in Illiyyin, a specific counterpart to the wicked record in 83:7.
terra: The earth is stretched out before casting out what lies within it, preparing a level ground for the release described in 84:4.
terra: The earth casts out what is inside it and empties, continuing the section's ground image into the resurrection release.
terra: The human labors toward the Lord and will meet Him, making the body's whole exertion terminate in return and encounter.
terra: When the Quran is recited, the addressees do not prostrate; refusal to lower the body before revelation becomes a sign of the deeper fall.
terra: The next ayah identifies the refusal as denial, explicitly tying bodily non-prostration to the same تكذيب challenged in surah 95.

luna: The section reads مَمْنُون as “cut off”; this verse gives believers who do good an أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, directly echoing the unbroken reward promised in 95:6. | terra: This ayah exactly repeats both the exception for those who believe and do good and the promise أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ.
terra: إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ attributes both origination and repetition to the same agent, a compact statement of the section's creation-return relation.

luna: The section’s root note describes تقويم as setting something upright and removing its crookedness; this verse says God created and proportioned, a direct lexical and bodily parallel. | terra: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ states in compact form that creation includes setting in due proportion, the closest non-root equivalent of takwīm's forming work.

luna: The section’s image is of a body given its measure; this next verse says God determined and guided after creating and proportioning in 87:2. | terra: After creating and proportioning in 87:2, God measures and guides; fitting form is joined to an assigned measure and course.
luna: The section contrasts the lowered human with the faithful exception; this verse says the one who purifies himself succeeds, giving a specific positive path alongside the low outcome.
luna: The section’s exception is for those who believe and do good; this next verse specifies remembering the Lord and praying as acts of the successful person in 87:14.

luna: The section’s body is lowered while its faithful exception receives a lasting reward; this verse says people prefer the nearer life, which 87:17 contrasts with the lasting Hereafter. | terra: People prefer the worldly life, a specific choice of the nearer and passing condition that parallels clinging to earth.

luna: The section promises a reward not cut off; this next verse says the Hereafter is better and more lasting than the nearer life, completing 87:16. | terra: The Hereafter is better and more enduring, stating the lasting counterpart to the section's uncut reward.
luna: The section’s body is sent to the lowest; this verse depicts faces humbled and exhausted, the first group in a passage that contrasts their Fire with the elevated garden of 88:10.
luna: The section’s low outcome for some is set against its faithful exception; this verse opens the opposing group with faces made glad and ease, before 88:10 locates them in a lofty garden.
luna: The section places lowliness beside an enduring reward; this verse gives the opposing group a “lofty garden,” completing the contrast begun with the humbled faces in 88:2.

luna: The section’s secondary بلد sense pictures a camel placing its chest on the ground; this verse asks people to look at the camel’s creation, focusing on the same animal’s bodily form without depicting its kneeling.
luna: The section’s image turns on upright height and support; this next verse asks how the sky was raised, continuing 88:17’s invitation to observe created forms.
luna: The section’s dictionary form قِوَام names what keeps a thing upright; this next verse asks how mountains were set firm, continuing the created-order scene of 88:17 and 88:18.
luna: The section connects the body to the ground; this next verse asks how the earth was spread out, completing the sequence of created forms in 88:17, 88:18, and 88:19.
terra: Iram is identified with lofty pillars, the very structural object named in the section as the support that holds something upright.

luna: Like 95:3, this oath names “this city”; the same surah later says in 90:4 that God created the human in hardship, placing the human image under the city’s setting. | terra: لَآ أُقْسِمُ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ repeats the oath by 'this city,' activating the same named place before the bodily meanings the section hears beneath balad.
terra: The Prophet is described in relation to 'this city,' continuing 90:1's oath and locating the addressee within the same named ground; the precise nuance of حِلٌّ is not relied upon here.
terra: مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ pictures a destitute person pressed into dust, a concrete meeting of low social rank and bodily nearness to earth.

luna: The section speaks of a human formed in the best proportion; this verse swears by the soul and the One who proportioned it, beginning a passage about the soul’s two directions. | terra: The oath by the soul and the One who proportioned it moves the section's fitted form inward, from bodily balance to the human self.

luna: The section’s image turns from formed humanity to distinct outcomes; this next verse says the soul is shown its wickedness and its piety, continuing the proportioning in 91:7. | terra: The proportioned self is shown both its wickedness and its piety, explaining how one created form opens toward opposed moral ranks.

luna: The section reserves an enduring reward for believers who do good; this next verse says the one who purifies the soul succeeds, the positive direction named in 91:8. | terra: Success belongs to the one who purifies the proportioned self, a close ethical counterpart to the section's faithful exception.

luna: The section contrasts a low outcome with the faithful exception; this next verse says the one who corrupts the soul fails, opposite the purification and success in 91:9. | terra: Failure belongs to the one who corrupts or buries the self, giving the moral fall an earthward verb after the self's proportioning.
terra: A person's wealth will not avail إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ, when he falls; material support fails at the decisive downward movement.
terra: Creation of the human from a clinging clot begins a short passage that soon shows the created person imagining himself independent.
terra: كَلَّآ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَيَطْغَىٰ marks the formed human's moral overreach, the start of the downward turn completed by the next ayat.
terra: The human transgresses because he sees himself as self-sufficient, a direct spiritual denial of the section's claim that standing always depends on a sustaining power.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ restores the dependence denied in 96:7 by naming the unavoidable return to the Lord.
terra: The command وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب makes going down to the ground the means of drawing near, reversing any simple equation of physical height with spiritual rank.

luna: The section places the human’s lowest outcome beside an exception; this verse calls disbelievers the worst of created beings, and its next verse supplies the opposite group. | terra: The section cites deniers as شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ, making moral response turn created beings toward the worst rank.

luna: The section’s exception is for those who believe and do good; this next verse calls such people the best of created beings, completing the worst/best contrast begun in 98:6. | terra: The section's faithful exception is mirrored by believers who do good becoming خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ, the opposite human rank to 98:6.
terra: The earth is shaken with its final convulsion before bringing out its burdens, so the supporting ground itself moves at bodily emergence.
terra: The earth brings out its burdens, a compact image of buried bodies no longer remaining below.
terra: The contents of the graves are scattered out, directly continuing the section's grave-ground image into bodily exposure at judgment.
luna: The section sends a human down to the lowest; this verse calls the abyss his “mother” when his scales are light, a concrete image of a low final destination.
terra: Worldly rivalry continues until people visit the graves; bodily arrival in cemetery-ground terminates the self-exalting contest.
terra: إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ gives another universal low outcome for humanity, whose exception is supplied by the next ayah.
terra: The exception for faith, good works, truth, and patience closely parallels the section's movement from humanity's descent to those exempted through faith and deeds.
terra: The Fire closes upon its inmates in extended columns; a pillar that ordinarily supports becomes part of the enclosure of the fallen.
terra: The Lord of the House feeds people against hunger and secures them against fear, specifying the bodily sustenance contained in the image of a secure city.
